MANDARIN — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MANDARIN
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening for Gist, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Gist.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Gist.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Gist.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Gist.

2. When practising Phonological Awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.

3. When practising Guided Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Guided Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Guided Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Guided Reading.

4. When practising Reading Aloud, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Aloud.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Aloud.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading Aloud.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading Aloud.

5. In MANDARIN, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Only memorise without using the language
   B. Avoid speaking to classmates
   C. Mix random languages with no purpose
   D. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day

6. When practising Imitative Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Imitative Speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Imitative Speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative Speaking.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
7. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for Gist and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

8. In three clear sentences, explain Imitative Speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

9. In three clear sentences, explain Reading Aloud and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

10. In three clear sentences, explain Reading Aloud and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

11. In three clear sentences, explain Reading Aloud and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
